newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico readies anti-money laundering handbook.
newsitem.headline: Mexico readies anti-money laundering handbook.

text.p: A handbook explaining how to detect narco-dollars being laundered through the financial system will be ready for local bankers in two week's time, a Mexican finance official said on Thursday.

"The manual we are working on...has a chapter on the identification of clients, a chapter on suspicious operations and we hope that it will be finished this week," a Mexican finance ministry official told reporters.
Mexico's fiscal attorney general Ismael Gomez said the ministry was planning to present the manuals on September 1.
Based on a guide produced by the Mexican Bankers' Association and the Banking and Securities Commission, the manual ought to be in use in all Mexican financial institutions by January, he said.
Gomez also said that, since 1994, the finance ministry had carried out around 200 money-laundering investigations, of which 30 had been brought before the federal Attorney General's Office.
Of those 30, 17 cases were under investigation and the remainder assigned to different judges. Four of the latter cases had ended in sentencing, Gomez said.
Suspicious cases would typically be signalled by inconsistency in client behaviour or by transactions greater than $10,000, or its equivalent in any currency, he added.
